solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lois stripped to take part in wild East German threesome

indicators.note: wild letters run out of control into a new order
a name stripped of its outer layers keeps only its inside letters

parts.note: taken as written, used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A woman named Lois, undressed, joins an East German couple in a racy liaison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' leaves OI from Lois; 'wild' shuffles OI with EASTGERMAN. 'to take part in' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names a domestic or sexual arrangement involving three people, a trio.

clue.text: Steven in Grimsby keeping late hours

indicators.note: the words Steven in Grimsby keep the required letters within them

explanation.surface: A man named Steven, living in the Lincolnshire fishing town of Grimsby, stays up late.
explanation.definitionFit: Late hours of the day, after the afternoon, form the time before night.

clue.text: Renegade disguised as teapot

indicators.note: a disguise changes how something looks, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traitor goes about in disguise as a piece of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who abandons a faith or cause is a turncoat or renegade.

clue.text: Extremities and backsides of these men developed chilblains

indicators.note: the backsides of words are their final letters

explanation.surface: Cold feet and cold bottoms: these men have chilblains in awkward places.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: extremities are the far tips or terminal points of something.

clue.text: It carries refreshments, stereotypically revolting but not spicy

indicators.note: revolting means the letters of stereotypically are rearranged, and but not says the letters of spicy are taken away from that pool

explanation.surface: Bland English food, stereotypically, is revolting yet never spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take SPICY out of STEREOTYPICALLY and rearrange the ten letters left, TERETOALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled trolley is a cart pushed around to serve cups and cakes in an office or train.

clue.text: Love excellent series finale

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
mega is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A fan loves the brilliant last episode of a TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet, so the end of the series of letters.

clue.text: Saint from Spain concealing suffering inside

indicators.note: Spain concealing its suffering means that part of the word is hidden away and dropped

parts.note: suffering is pain
inside means within

explanation.surface: A holy man from Spain hides the pain he is feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' removes PAIN from SPAIN, leaving S. 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: St Swithin was a ninth-century Bishop of Winchester; his July feast day is linked with rain in English folklore.

clue.text: Biography leads to passionate readers hosting book club

parts.note: a biography is a life

indicators.note: the two letters host, or hold, the other piece between them
leads are the opening letters of words

parts.note: to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: A biography leads keen readers to start a book club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' gives P and R from passionate readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a lifebuoy, a life preserver is a short weighted cudgel, a club for self-defence.

clue.text: Those expecting inheritance hire wanton to exhaust dad, perhaps

indicators.note: wanton means unrestrained, so the letters of hire run loose

parts.note: to sap is to exhaust or drain
a dad is an example of a parent

explanation.surface: Greedy children hire a loose woman to wear their father out.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirs apparent are successors certain to inherit, so they await their legacy.

clue.text: Reportedly observe shrew freezing

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: to observe is to eye, and a shrew is a scold, a nagging woman

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have watched a small mammal that was frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: EYE SCOLD said aloud runs together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something freezing is extremely chilly, as cold as frozen water.

clue.text: Base in Wiesbaden, inexplicably

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the following words

explanation.surface: A military base inside the German city of Wiesbaden exists for no clear reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inexplicably' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters sit in plain order across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A base in biochemistry is one of the nucleotide components of DNA; this is one of the four.

clue.text: Are real male chauvinists ignoring boundaries?

indicators.note: boundaries are the outside letters, here ignored and dropped

parts.note: male chauvinists are sexists

explanation.surface: A question whether chauvinist men really are as bad, disregarding limits of decency.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural verb synonym: things that are real have being or presence in the world.

clue.text: British faculty inspiring the rest

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: hearing is a faculty, and the ear is its organ

explanation.surface: A British university department motivates the remainder of the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is part of the wordplay, not the article of 'the rest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a short pause to recover, a break from effort.

clue.text: Angry teen gang involving setter in battle

indicators.note: involving means the first piece takes in the second
angry suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: An angry gang of teenagers drags the crossword setter into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry' rearranges TEENGANG to ENGAGENT, which takes in ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an engagement in military use is a fight between opposing forces.

clue.text: Doctor and husband clash in corner of square

parts.note: to doctor is to rig or falsify
to tangle with someone is to clash with them

explanation.surface: A physician and a married man get into a fight in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb here, meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Each corner of a square is a ninety-degree turn, the angle measuring ninety degrees.

clue.text: Old South American tattooist on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen in writing

parts.note: a tattooist inks skin, so is an inker

explanation.surface: A tattoo artist is interviewed on a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas ruled an Andean empire in Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Wheeling discontented granny over allotment

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second
discontented means emptied of its contents, leaving just the outer letters

parts.note: an allotment is a ration, a share allotted

explanation.surface: An unhappy grandmother fusses over her vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is also a British rented garden plot, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wheeling and gyration both mean turning round in circles.

clue.text: Text about Ursula's initial problems at primary school

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece

parts.note: SMS is a phone text message

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of Ursula's

explanation.surface: A message mentions young Ursula's early difficulties at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic exercises set for young children are the classic schoolroom questions.

clue.text: Garment of one inferior to most of humanity

indicators.note: inferior to means lower down, so in a down clue the piece comes beneath
most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: humanity is mankind
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is described as beneath most of the human race.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimpy one-piece swimsuit for men, popularised by the comedy film Borat.

clue.text: Dodgy playmates pocketing fine lighter of mine

indicators.note: pocketing means taking the other piece inside
dodgy means unreliable or shifty, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Shady companions steal a nice cigarette lighter belonging to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges PLAYMATES, which takes in F.
explanation.definitionFit: The Davy lamp lit coal mines without igniting firedamp gas, lighting the mine.

clue.text: Earthy construction workers make Xanthe inwardly sick

indicators.note: inwardly means only the inner letters of Xanthe are taken

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: Building labourers make a woman named Xanthe feel sick to her stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' are ants, so the definition is what ants build from soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants build a mound of soil as their nest, an earthen structure.

clue.text: Famous US city, three quarters Democrat

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
quarters are compass points; here west, north and east

explanation.surface: A well-known American city is three-quarters Democrat voters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone famous is celebrated or widely known.

clue.text: Chap pressing suit with expression of alarm

parts.note: ooer is a British exclamation of mock alarm or surprise

explanation.surface: A man ironing a suit cries out in alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: To press one's suit is to court someone, not iron clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A man courting a woman pursues her affections, which old usage called pressing his suit.

clue.text: Hotel twice leaving Hal the right change

indicators.note: leaving means those letters depart from the words that follow
twice means the letter is taken two times

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel twice leaves Hal with the right change from his bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym verb: to change something is to modify or adjust it.

clue.text: Southern Burmese perhaps get lost

parts.note: a Burmese is a breed of cat

explanation.surface: A southern Burmese person might lose their way.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperative telling someone to go away, as said to shoo an animal.

clue.text: Typical example of English goody-goody, in my opinion

parts.note: pi is British slang short for pious, priggishly virtuous
to me means in my opinion

explanation.surface: A speaker thinks an English prig is a classic instance of the type.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a perfect embodiment of a class or quality.

clue.text: Male favourite banned from tournament for it

indicators.note: banned from means these letters are kept out of the word

parts.note: a tournament is a competition
a favourite is a pet

explanation.surface: A top male seed is thrown out of a tournament for something he did.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' is a coy euphemism for sex, and this word means sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Irish girl experiencing pins and needles in irksome way

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
pins and needles is a prickling feeling, so tingly

explanation.surface: An Irish girl who has pins and needles behaves in an annoying manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: done in an irksome way is done annoyingly or vexingly.
